speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help me determine the cause, can you describe exactly what kind of pain or discomfort you feel and where it is located?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the relief of symptoms after voiding and pain with intercourse are significant clues. To better assess the potential for interstitial cystitis or other pelvic floor issues, how would you describe the nature of the pain (e.g., pressure, burning, cramping) and is it worse when your bladder is full?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome.

The history of symptoms worsening with bladder fullness, relief after voiding, lack of fever, and the absence of response to antibiotics strongly points away from a simple urinary tract infection. The pain with intercourse also supports a diagnosis involving the bladder wall or pelvic floor rather than a typical UTI.
